answer: Each seat registers one licensed vessel and a home wharf before the season. The seed names an inlet and a two-hour tide window; the boat must land inside it after fishing past the canyon wall. A weighmaster signs a docket listing hull, species, kilos and landing minute, and harbour AIS must show that hull crossing the inlet mouth. Seats sharing a hull, licence or docket serial fold into one vote at a 45,000 POA forfeit. Licence, survey and fuel cost near $2,650 per landing, so a thousand clones need a thousand seaworthy boats. Paper fleets sink when a weighmaster asks for the hull.
